name: TSI Careers – Job Openings & Application Form
author: TSI Digital Solution

sections.description:
TSI Careers turns any page of your site into a careers page. List your open positions, let candidates apply with a clean form and a CV upload, and follow up from a simple applicant inbox in your dashboard. Everything stays on your own website.

What you get

  • Job openings with type (Staff or Freelance), department, location, remote flag, salary indication and an application deadline. Jobs close automatically after the deadline.
  • A complete application form: contact details, links, experience, availability, rate expectation, cover letter and up to three file uploads (PDF, Word, image or ZIP).
  • Applicant inbox: search, filter by status or position, sort, bulk actions, and a detail view for every application. Statuses: New, Reviewing, Interview, Hired, Rejected, Archived.
  • Email notification to one or more addresses, with the CV attached and a Reply-To set to the applicant.
  • Three ways to show it: the [tsi_careers] shortcode, a block, and an Elementor widget.
  • Your branding: logo, two colours, heading and intro text. The text colour adapts to your main colour so buttons stay readable.
  • Spam protection that works with page caching: hidden field, minimum fill time and a per-visitor rate limit. Works next to TSI Visitor Blocker.
  • Privacy tools: consent checkbox with a record of when it was given, a link to your privacy policy, and an option to restrict applications to one country or phone prefix.
  • Accessible and fast: keyboard-friendly, screen-reader labels, reduced-motion support, loads its files only on pages that show the careers widget. No external fonts or scripts.
  • Developer friendly: template overrides from your theme, and filters and actions for extending the form, validation, emails and the admin.

How it works

  1. Open Settings → TSI Careers and add your vacancies under the Job Openings tab.
  2. Place [tsi_careers] on a page, or use the TSI Careers block or Elementor widget.
  3. Applications arrive by email and appear under Settings → TSI Careers → Applications.

Shortcode

  • [tsi_careers] shows all open positions and the form.
  • [tsi_careers type="freelance"] shows only one type of position (staff or freelance).
  • [tsi_careers max_width="800px"] limits the width.

Privacy

Applications contain personal data that you collect and are responsible for. The plugin stores each application (name, email, phone, country, optional links and details, cover letter and the names of uploaded files) in your own database, together with a record of the consent given. Uploaded files are emailed to you and are not kept on your server. The visitor IP address is never stored; for rate limiting a one-way hash is kept in a temporary value for up to one hour. Mention job applications in your privacy policy and select that page in the plugin settings.

External services

This plugin does not connect to any external service and loads no third-party scripts, fonts or tracking.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the tsi-careers folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate TSI Careers – Job Openings & Application Form.
  3. Open Settings → TSI Careers → Settings and set the notification email, logo and colours.
  4. Add jobs under the Job Openings tab, then place the [tsi_careers] shortcode on a page.
sections.faq:
Where do the CVs go?

Files are attached to the notification email and are not stored on your website. The Applications screen lists the file names.

Does it create a page for every job?

Not in this version. Jobs are shown as cards with a full description on one page.

Can I limit applications to one country?

Yes. In the Settings tab, under Application form, you can set a country and a phone prefix. Both are checked in the browser and again on the server.

Will it work with a caching plugin?

Yes. The security token is requested when the form is sent, so a cached copy of the page never carries a stale one.

Can I change the look of the cards and the form?

Set your colours in the settings, or copy the files from the plugin templates folder to a folder named tsi-careers in your theme and edit them.

I used the earlier “TSI Careers – Hiring” version.

Deactivate the old plugin and activate this one, then click “Import data now” under Settings → TSI Careers. The import only copies your job openings, applications and settings. The old data is not changed, so you can go back to the old plugin at any time.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

Nothing, unless you tick “Remove all job openings, applications and settings” in the settings first.
sections.changelog:
1.2.6

  • First release on WordPress.org. Complete restructure of the 1.0 and 1.1 builds.
  • New: applicant inbox with search, status and position filters, sorting, pagination and bulk actions.
  • New: Gutenberg block, in addition to the shortcode and the Elementor widget.
  • New: consent checkbox with a stored consent record, privacy policy link, optional required CV, and a switch for general applications.
  • New: spam protection that works with page caching (hidden field, minimum fill time, rate limit). Detects TSI Visitor Blocker.
  • New: jobs close automatically after their deadline; the Applications column on the job list links to the matching applications.
  • New: multiple notification recipients, and a notice when an email could not be sent.
  • New: theme template overrides, translation-ready strings, and a Help page.
  • New: extension points (filters and actions) for add-ons.
  • Improved: job title and type are read from the database on submit instead of the request; uploaded files are checked on the server and rejected files are reported to the applicant.
  • Improved: no external fonts; the form inherits your theme font. Accessible markup, keyboard support and reduced-motion support.
  • Improved: settings use the WordPress Settings API; all admin styles and scripts are enqueued files.
  • Improved: opt-in uninstall routine (it only removes this plugin’s own data), and an Import button that copies data from earlier builds without changing it.
